body:
FOUND DURING T186's curse slice, 2026-08-19. Criterion 11 itself is MET and green: cursing one bound
law retires that law only, and the retirement survives a subsequent poll. This ticket is the piece
BEYOND the criterion that I added and could not finish.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK: `curseChannelLaw(channel, living, { lift: true })`. It strikes the curse record
using the substrate's real negation shape (makeNegationClaims — an earlier draft hand-rolled a
"negates" pointer, which appended cleanly and changed nothing, and that bug IS fixed). The next poll
still does not re-bless.

THE EVIDENCE, and it narrows the search: the living name is never re-attempted at all. `parked` comes
back EMPTY, so the blessing is not refusing — the skip is happening upstream, in the cursed-set
filter. Either the strike is not binding (an authority question) or `cursesOf` is reading a stale
set. Diagnosed no further; the loop moved on rather than burn an iteration on a nice-to-have.

WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: a curse the operator cannot lift is a one-way door on a REVERSIBLE control.
§46's whole toggle design separates reversible acts (freeze, unbless, curse) from the irreversible one
(drop). A curse that cannot be undone quietly joins the wrong group, and an operator who learns that
the hard way has lost a peer's law with only a re-federation to recover it.

RAILS: the skipped rail in test/federation/curse-durable.test.ts is written and ready — un-skip it.
Two-sided: lifting a curse on one law must not lift it on a channel-mate that is also cursed.

DO NOT ship `lift` in any doc, help text, or tool description as working until that rail is green.
title: Lifting a curse does not re-bless — the cursed name is never re-attempted
